record.summary: Proposed gas-powered data centre campus on Crown land about 19 km south of Swan Hills, Alberta, in Big Lakes County. Kiwetinohk Energy first proposed the roughly 460 MW Black Bear combined-cycle plant in 2024 and received a federal decision that no impact assessment was needed; Teton Digital has since taken it up as the power source for about 1,500 acres of adjacent data centre land. Teton describes a 466 MW first phase with a path to about 3 GW, compute online as early as 2027 using grid power, and the full plant running in Q3 2028. Alberta's project inventory lists it as proposed.

sources.title: Planetel reports completion of TERRA-1 in Padua
sources.summary: Planetel reports 1,200 m² of floor area for TERRA-1. At full operation it expects capacity for up to 120 racks and 1 MW of power. The filing does not specify how much of that power would serve IT equipment.

extraction.status_basis: On PDF page 3, In-Site founder Pietro Matteo Foglio describes working on the named Padua data centre from design through completion. Planetel’s CEO describes the conversion of its own industrial building.
extraction.date_semantics: Completion was reported by 18 November. An exact works completion date, first customer or service commencement is unspecified.
extraction.property: Planetel Hub, Via Vigonovese 52, Padua. Site-specific certificate supplies the 52A suffix.

metrics.floor_area: 1,200 m² reported for TERRA-1. The issuer does not break out technical white space.
metrics.racks: Up to 120 racks at full operation. Installed or occupied rack count is unknown.
metrics.capacity: 1 MW at full operation, without a stated IT-load or utility-input basis. No energized or measured MW figure is assigned.

sources.title: Bureau Veritas design certificate IT346993-1 identifies the Padua data centre
sources.summary: The certificate identifies the data-centre address as Via della Meccanica 2 / Via Vigonovese 52A in Padua.

extraction.scope: Historical design validation only. The certificate expiry date was 22 October 2026. Used solely to identify the site.
